recipes.name: Simple Beef Short Ribs
ingredients_raw: 1 (12 fluid ounce) can or bottle stout beer

steps.text: Season ribs with salt and pepper. Dredge in flour until coated; shake off excess.
Heat olive oil and butter in a Dutch oven or large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook ribs until browned, about 5 minutes per side. Remove ribs and set aside.

Add onion and garlic to the pot; cook and stir until onion is tender, about 5 minutes. Return ribs to the pot; pour in beer while scraping the browned bits of food off the bottom of the pot. Pour in beef stock.
Cover and simmer over low heat until ribs are very tender, about 2 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Simple Beef Short Ribs
raw_recipe.description: This beef short ribs recipe braises beef ribs in stout beer with broth, onion, and garlic until fall-off-the-bone tender for a delicious one-pot meal.

video.description: Looking for a great recipe for beef short ribs? Look no further. In this video, we'll show you how to sear the ribs first, and then simmer them with onions, garlic, beer, and beef broth until perfectly tender.

review.reviewBody: Loved this recipe! It was simple! I made the ribs in my crockpot. I added a couple of extra cloves of garlic cause that's what we like. The juice from the ribs made an outstanding gravy for potatoes! Yummy!!!
Like other reviewers, I added extra garlic and the second time, I tossed in a few thyme sprigs. I also put it in the oven at 275 until it was done. This is SUCH a satisfying dish!
I increased the braising time to further tenderize the meat. Also added potatoes and carrots for the last 30 minutes. Love the simplicity!

Was very surprised despite all the good reviews. I did adjust for our family. I used almond flour seasoned with rosemary, garlic powder, pepper and paprika. I used a crockpot on low for 6 hours adding potatoes and carrots the last 45 min. My crockpot runs hot, thus the cut in time. I used Sierra Nevada Stout. I used 2 cups of beef bone broth and 2 cups of chicken broth. It was melt in your mouth and so flavorful. I followed others advice and was heavy handed on the salt when seasoning the meat. I also used the broth afterwards to make a delicious gravy. I think next time I will serve with mashed potatoes and green beans. This will definitely be a repeat for us and dinner guests. It's that good.

I boiled for 2 hours. Placed beef ribs on a baking pan braised with BBQ sauce. Oven on 350 degrees baked for 35 minutes. My first time cooking beef ribs because my daughter n law doesn't eat pork. Beef ribs were amazing and I am keeping this recipe for future cookouts. Thank you so much 💓 💗 💛 Then I used the beer/beef stock to cook my cabbage 😋 again because I couldn't used bacon in the cabbage 😋 I got 2 for the price of 1!!!

Really good!! I followed the recipe, except I used regular beer because that was all I had. About 50 minutes before beef was done, I added celery and carrots. And about 40 minutes prior to it finishing, I added quartered potatoes. It was all so yummy! I will definitely make this recipe again!!
I used shallots instead of onions, added Sherry vinegar as a deglazer, used 17 oz of beef stock, and a T of tomato paste. It cooked down and made a lovely sauce.

I don't do much cooking since my husband is a vegetarian and cooks his own meals 90% of the time. But I wanted to try these boneless short ribs and this recipe was simple and did the trick. I had no garlic but I followed along and used shallot instead of onion/garlic and added parsley, rosemary, thyme and tarragon to flavor it up. I used a small Staub dutch oven - two firsts - my first short ribs and my first use of the Staub pot. For liquid, I used white wine and water with a vegetable bullion cube. Came out great, two small portions, one for tonight another for some other time plus lots of gravy left over. I was so excited they were tender I forgot to take a photo (sorry) haha). If I did it again I would make a larger amount and save some for a friend. Thank you Allrecipes!

This made an outstanding dinner! I made this recipe with Merlot wine rather than beer and I doubled the amount of ribs, used a large onion and 6 cloves of garlic. I served this over mashed potatoes and with green beans. It would, also, be good served with noodles. It came out so tender and delicious. Next time I will try adding some sour cream and perhaps mushrooms extending the sauce more. We have leftovers for lunch now - there were 2 large short ribs and 2 small ones in the packages that I bought so the small ribs will be lunch.

I have made this recipe many times. There are better but more complex recipes out there for short ribs. However, you can't beat this one for simplicity. For added flavor I sometimes reduced the broth to make a demi glace. I even made this in a dutch oven over a campfire. We have also used beef shin instead of short ribs because it was more economical and it was just as good. Stout does add some more flavor but I usually use the darkest beer I have around, typically Yuengling Lager. This is one of those recipes that you can easily be altered to your taste to make it your own.
I’m allergic to alcohol, so I used a bottle of IBC root beer and it turned out great. I thickened the gravy with some flour and extra beef broth and used that over mashed potatoes.
Cooked on the stovetop, about 2 hours. Used red wine instead of beer, added mushrooms, and it turned out rich and delicious. Served over mashed potatoes. There were NO leftovers!
it was very tasty, but there was a bit of a strange taste, I am thinking it was the dark beer as I am not a beer drinker. Will make this again using somethin different.

I made this last night. Doubled the recipe and used a baby black box of Pinot Noir... instead of beer...it was awesome...I followed the recipe to the t and used a bit of fresh ground pepper and fresh ground salt for the plate...just a touch..my husband has a culinary degree (I do not have his last name so don't try to find him..haha) from a blue ribbon school and he was super impressed said it could have been served in a 3 star restaurant...high praise..j.s And I'm an average cook..I don't burn water and can make a rue but.. definitely NOT a chef...this was easy to follow and super simple to execute..do take the time to pre prepare all the ingredients in my opinion...(Just put stuff in those annoying little storage cups that nobody uses and comes with the stuff we actually use)..makes it easier
Red wine!!!
It was a little bland for my taste, but will try again with some modifications.
Made it in the slow cooker, but followed the rest of the recipe. Loved every bite.
Great simple recipe, the only difference, I cooked it on my pressurer cooker.

I made this recipe using beef broth and some sherry as I did not have beer on hand. I also added some mushrooms with the onions and garlic. The meat turned out really tender and flavorful. I would thicken the stock a little bit next time before serving.
That's the way I do it. Easy peasy thanks
